current.text: Jaylen Brown is gone from Boston. Jayson Tatum and Paul George are on the team, and George is the clear number two option behind Tatum.
Experts expect his usage and time on the ball to drop because he moves from second option to third option behind Tatum and George.
One expert expects him to play under 34 minutes per game.
Both Boston previews project him as a starting guard.
He has played in the preseason.
Experts expect his FG% to improve this season, with more catch-and-shoot looks next to Tatum and George, who share the ball more than Brown did.

In category leagues, experts value him around rank 40 to 50 or round 4. They call picks in the low 30s a little early and ESPN's top 20 rank absurd. They see him as more likely to fall short of a Fantrax ADP of 34 than to reach it.
In auctions, Josh values him in the mid 20s. He calls a 14 USD price an unbelievable steal.
Boston has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league. Experts say this mainly affects Paul George and Mitchell Robinson.
Boston plays 4, 3 and 4 games in fantasy playoff weeks 19 to 21. That is one game short of the maximum, with three back-to-backs in that window.
Experts project Boston to be better than last season, with about 48 wins.

durable.text: Experts call him an excellent steals and blocks player. His blocks are far above other guards.
FG% is his weak category. He shoots a low percentage on real volume, so he drags down a team's FG%.
He is worth much more in category leagues than in points leagues.

note: Experts put his 9-cat value around rank 40 to 50 and his auction value in the mid 20s. That matches Yahoo's 25 USD, not ESPN's 42 USD or the 30 USD he cost in our league last season. A price in the mid teens, close to Yahoo's 14.9 USD average cost, is a bargain. He fits punt FG% builds best because his threes, FT%, assists and guard-level blocks all help. Early in the season, check whether his FG% climbs back above 40% and whether his minutes and usage hold up next to Tatum and George.
